topics: General Introduction –introduction to boundary value problems
approximate numerical solutions for solving differential equations
polynomial approximations for 1D and 2D  elements using Lagrange polynomials
CST, LST and bilinear rectangular elements
Variational approach and weighted residual approach
formulation of element equations for 1D bar element, 1D beam element and CST element.
Development of stiffness matrix for bar element and beam element
Discussion of modelling and analysis using recent commercial finite element software packages

partA.description: 2 Questions from each module.  Total of 8 Questions, each carrying 3 marks

partB.description: Each question carries 9 marks.  Two questions will be given from each module, out of which 1 question should be answered.  Each question can have a maximum of 3 sub divisions.

courseOutcomes.description: Understand the basic features of boundary value problems and methods to solve them
Get familiar with the basic element types and shape functions so as to identify and choose suitable elements to solve a particular problem.
Understand the fundamental concept of the finite element method and develop the ability to generate the governing FE equations for systems governed by partial differential equations
Understand the concepts of isoparametric elements and apply it for problems in structural engineering
Apply numerical integration procedures as a tool to solve mathematical models in FEM
